reasoning: The block's description of the evidence is accurate and the evidence does not decide the first end. EO 6254 (August 19, 1933; held APP common-crawl transcription, hash and page record match) approves the Iron and Steel code in one paragraph. The held EO 6730 text (May 30, 1934; APP page record matches) approves 'said amendments' and 'said Code as amended by said amendments'. It then calls the result 'said revised Code incorporating said amendments to become effective on June 11, 1934, prior to which effective date the Code of Fair Competition approved August 19, 1933, shall continue in full force and effect.' The quotations in the block match the held bytes. Nothing in the text expressly revokes, cancels or supersedes the 1933 approval. The negative implication of 'prior to which ... shall continue' and the words 'revised Code' support a replacement reading. The words 'amendments to said Code' and 'said Code as amended' support a continuing-approval-as-amended reading. The shared analysis treats an amending order as a later event 'unless its text replaces the code or revokes or cancels the approval', so the question turns on exactly this wording and the analysis does not settle it. Other held texts naming the code do not decide it either: EO 6751 (1934), EO 7085 (1935) and EO 7010-H refer to 'the Code of Fair Competition for the Iron and Steel Industry' without distinguishing versions, and the register and WPA list show only EO 6254 and EO 6730 for this code. The two readings give different first ends (1934-06-11 versus 1935-06-14). Under the 2026-10-28 ruling an endpoint needs a reason, and disclosure does not supply one. Holding the order open is therefore supported. I do not decide which reading is correct.

reasoning: Supported on the custody ground. The second stated reason is accurate, but on its own it is not a reason to block. Custody: the only held text of EO 6438 (Hotel code, November 17, 1933) is the APP transcription with sha256 90c8b2ec..., captured by the Wayback Machine on 2023-09-04. MIRROR_SOURCES and MIRROR_DOCUMENTS record route archive/wayback and an id_ wayback_url with no WARC location, and note that the raw capture bytes are hashed but not committed. The clause-drafts copy derives from the same capture, and no other held text (FR, Hathi, ProQuest or Wikisource) carries this order. In checker.py, such a source passes custody only by re-hashing the bytes from a verified cache or by re-downloading the Wayback capture. Otherwise it is custody_record_only, a skip that COMPLETION.md keeps as a pass_with_unverified exception that is not promoted. In an offline checker run the Wayback bytes cannot be re-fetched. I did not open the kit cache outside REPO, so I have not confirmed whether verified bytes for the other orders' common-crawl captures sit there. The custody statement is consistent with the code and the records. EO 6620-B: the held text (APP common-crawl, page record matches, dated February 26, 1934; WPA list: 'E. O. 6438 ... amended to delete two specified conditions') reads 'do modify my order of November 17, 1933 ... by striking therefrom the conditions numbered two (2) and three (3).' That is accurate and is an earlier, held end for clauses (2) and (3). It is resolvable evidence rather than a block, and it leaves the lead approval with its article IV 1(d) exception and condition (1) to the June 14, 1935 analysis. The order also has a number collision: APP and the register hold EO 6438-A (a civil-service appointment waiver) under the same number. The register and the WPA list identify EO:6438 as the Hotel code, so identity is confirmable, but a filed claim must cite the right text.
